title: DiagnosisReport
description: Durable artifact produced by `restoreLesson diagnose` and appended to by `restore-english`, `apply`, and `verify`. Its existence, matching diagnosisId, and verified reportChecksum are the machine-checked precondition for apply (FR-005). MUST NOT contain credentials: no connection URL, password, SSH host, or secrets.json content. Written mode 0600 into a 0700 directory.

diagnosisChecksum.description: SHA-256 over ONLY the diagnosis-produced fields (identity, affectedLessons, languageIdentityChecks, mappings, findings, perLanguageCounts, blastRadius, plannedWrites, conflicts). Computed once by `diagnose` and NEVER recomputed. languageIdentityChecks is in the frozen set because restore-english and apply ASSERT it from the report rather than re-running the cross-database join (I25); covered by reportChecksum alone, the I22 guard would rest on a checksum recomputed at every append. This is the human-review gate: it proves the diagnosis being applied is the one reviewed at the runbook's step-4 gate (I13).

reportChecksum.description: SHA-256 over the canonical serialisation of the whole report body with this field excluded. Recomputed on every append, so it only detects tampering since the last tool write — it cannot serve as the review gate on its own. Re-verified by every write subcommand (I13); mismatch aborts with exit 20.

productionFingerprint.description: Identity evidence for the production database the diagnosis ran against (I13). databaseName is hard-gated; the count/max fields are evidence and are reported on change, since translator activity legitimately moves them.

expectedBumpCount.description: 1 for the first diagnosis; 1 + versions bumped by this tool for any later one (read from the prior report's englishRestore). The stop-and-re-review warning fires when bumpCount !== expectedBumpCount, so re-diagnosing after a legitimate English restore (bumpCount 2, snapshotAnchored) does not alarm on its own happy path.

knownBadVersions.description: Lesson versions that must never be re-uploaded — [158] for this incident. PINNED at first diagnosis and carried forward; never derived from the live production version, which after the restore-english bump to 159 would stop flagging the cover file and start flagging the file just correctly restored.

version.description: Parsed from the versioned filename. zeroPad(version, 2) pads to a MINIMUM width and never truncates, so the segment is variable width (v03, v157). Parse with v(\d+)\.odt$, not a fixed two-digit pattern.

isKnownBadUpload.description: True when this document's version is in the enclosing lesson's pinned knownBadVersions — i.e. it is the cover file that caused the incident (v158 for Luke 1-1). Hard-denied as --master-document with no override flag.

sha256.description: I23. Pinned at diagnose; restore-english re-hashes the file and aborts (22) on mismatch. The report is checksum-gated but the ODT on disk is not.

conflicts.description: Subset of findings with classification conflict or newerWork; left untouched, for human review (FR-008).

restored.description: Writes ACTUALLY applied, not planned. restored + driftSkipped equals this language's plannedWrites count.

driftSkipped.description: Apply only. Planned writes withheld because live production changed after the diagnosis (I11).

legacyLessonStringRowCounts.description: count(*) FROM tstrings WHERE lessonstringid IS NOT NULL — the second orphan vector, counted rather than assumed inert.

overwrote.description: Prior production value, now first in history. Null when the row was inserted.

driftSkips.description: Apply only. Planned writes withheld because the live production row no longer matches the diagnosis-time classification (I11). Any entry with benign === false makes apply exit 27; benign (intact) drift is recorded but does not.

benign.description: True iff reclassifiedAs === 'intact' — someone re-typed the exact text we were going to write. Recorded for the audit trail; does not trigger exit 27.

duplicateRowsBaseline.description: Diagnose. Duplicates that already existed before this tool touched anything — tstrings has had no unique constraint for the life of the database. Without this baseline, verify cannot tell a duplicate this tool created from one that was already there, and would default to blaming the restore in a document the client reads.

duplicateRows.description: Verify only. Result of the post-restore duplicate sweep (I19). The apply-time re-check narrows but cannot close the write race — tstrings has no unique constraint, so an absent row cannot be locked and adding one is outside this feature's scope. Detection is the honest compensation. Verify reports the DELTA against duplicateRowsBaseline; a non-empty delta exits 30.

priorDiagnosisId.description: Set when this diagnosis was run with --prior-report, carrying forward knownBadVersions and bump accounting from an earlier report (I20). Provenance for the drift-recovery loop.

applyState.description: Batch journal flushed atomically after EVERY per-language batch, so an interrupted apply still leaves a complete record of what was written (SC-004, I12). The temp file MUST be created in the SAME directory as the report — rename(2) is atomic only within a filesystem. The per-write log is also appended to a sibling journal which is never rewritten; appliedWrites is reconciled from it at the end and the journal wins on disagreement. The journal's path is DERIVED from the report's basename (<report-basename>.journal.jsonl), never the fixed name report.journal.jsonl (I27): the drift-recovery loop puts a second report in the same directory, so a fixed name would have two runs appending to one file — reconciling one run's writes into the other's report, and making --force-report's journal check refuse to create the second report at all. Every journal line carries its diagnosisId.

languageBatches.description: A throwing batch is marked failed with its failureMessage, flushed with the journal, and STOPS the run at exit 32 (I24) — no further languages are attempted.

scopedLanguageIds.description: --languages scope; null = whole corpus. verify reports languages outside the scope as 'not yet applied' rather than as zero-restore outcomes, and apply's computed --max-writes default is derived over the scoped languages only.

englishRestore.description: Written by restore-english, OR carried forward by diagnose --prior-report so that apply's precondition 8 stays satisfiable on the drift-recovery path (I26): English was restored under the earlier report, and the re-diagnosis writes to a new report path. Without the carry-forward, apply aborts 24 ("English master not yet restored") on a lesson that has been correctly restored.

carriedFromDiagnosisId.description: Null when this report's own restore-english produced the entry; the earlier report's diagnosisId when diagnose --prior-report carried it forward (I26). verify must not present a carried restore as this run's work, and --force-report's refusal to clobber an audit artifact keys on a SELF-PRODUCED entry only — keyed on presence alone, a drift-recovery report would be unoverwritable from the moment it is created while recording no writes of its own. It names the report that PERFORMED the restore: on a second drift recovery an already-carried entry keeps its original value rather than advancing to the intermediate report's id, so it never stops pointing at the run that actually touched production. priorDiagnosisId is the per-hop provenance and does advance.

dumpPath.description: This step's own pg_dump path. Not redundant with preApplyDumpPath (written by apply): this dump is the ONLY rollback route in the window between a successful English restore and apply, and it is credential-bearing, so it must be enumerated in the runbook's destruction step.

preApplyDumpPath.description: Path to the pg_dump -Fc file. The dump contains the WHOLE database, including better-auth user/account (Argon2id hashes), session, and invitation tables — written mode 0600 into a 0700 directory, never copied off the production host, deleted once the client confirms restoration.

languageIdentityChecks.description: I22. Cross-database evidence that a languageId denotes the same language on both sides. languages.languageId is a serial, like lessonId and masterId, yet every finding and write carries one bare value used on both sides; divergence would write one language's translations into another language's rows and no downstream guard would catch it. The join key is chosen at runtime, never assumed: languages.code is declared bare text (nullable, not unique), so diagnose tests code on BOTH databases for non-null and unique, falls back to testing name identically, and aborts (15) naming the offending rows when neither qualifies. Also fatal: id disagreement, many-to-one mapping, or a snapshot language with affected-lesson translations and no production counterpart. Verify-and-abort, never remap.

verification.description: Written by verify. mode must be durable, not just a console label: a later reader otherwise cannot tell whether after-figures came from a live snapshot comparison or from stored perLanguageCounts. clientReportWithheld pairs with exit 30 — the Markdown is always written, but on a non-empty duplicate delta its first heading is a DRAFT - DO NOT SEND banner.

coverage.description: partial when apply was --languages-scoped and languages with planned writes remain unapplied. A scoped apply does not satisfy SC-002, which is stated over every active language, so the client Markdown is headed INTERIM.

lessonStringId.description: Always null — restored rows use the shape all current write paths use.

history.description: Always empty: saveTStrings routes non-empty-history rows to UPDATE, which no-ops for rows that do not yet exist (research D6).
